items.title: AI基建放緩疑慮引爆晶片股殺盤！美光慘崩逾17%、Sandisk暴跌逾22%
items.title_en: AI Infrastructure Slowdown Fears Spark Chip Stock Sell‑off! Micron Crashes Over 17%, Sandisk Plummets Over 22%
paras: 美股半導體與人工智慧 (AI) 概念股週四 (5 日) 遭遇猛烈拋售，市場擔憂美國期中選舉後，資料中心建設將面臨更多許可與監管阻力，加上電價上漲引發政治壓力，可能拖慢 AI 基礎建設擴張。Sandisk (SNDK-US) 暴跌 22.26%，成為標普 500 指數表現最差成分股；美光 (MU-US)、超微 (AMD-US) 與威騰電子 (WDC-US) 跌幅均超過 17%。
《MarketWatch》報導，這波賣壓反映投資人重新評估 AI 建設速度，以及相關企業的獲利前景。分析師指出，政策走向尚未明朗，而近期部分科技業財報又未能穩固市場信心，使高度仰賴資料中心擴張的晶片、記憶體與儲存設備股承受沉重壓力。
費城半導體指數當天狂瀉 12.25%，創 2020 年 3 月 16 日以來最大單日跌幅。那斯達克綜合指數下跌 5.52%，創 2025 年 4 月以來最差單日表現，標普 500 指數也重挫 4.36%。
個股方面，美光下跌 17.46%，威騰電子下跌 17.35%，超微下跌 17.26%，希捷 (STX-US) 下跌 16.25%。晶片龍頭輝達 (NVDA-US) 收跌 9.26%，英特爾 (INTC-US) 則下挫 10.33%。
電價成選舉議題 市場憂資料中心擴張受阻
Maxim Group 分析師 Tom Forte 表示，投資人擔心，這次如「海嘯」般的期中選舉結果，可能使資料中心擴張速度放慢。
Forte 指出，兩黨都有不少候選人，針對選民對電價上漲的憂慮提出競選訴求。選舉落幕後，市場接下來將觀察，這些政治承諾是否真正轉化為拖慢資料中心建設的措施。
這意味著，投資人目前面對的是政策可能改變的風險，而非已經確定發生的建設縮減。資料中心許可、監管要求及地方政治阻力，最終會如何影響投資與施工時程，仍有待釐清。
Rosenblatt Securities 分析師 Kevin Cassidy 表示，政治人物最後會採取什麼行動，目前仍不清楚，但「投資人不喜歡不確定性」。
Jefferies 交易部門分析師 Jeffrey Favuzza 也指出，現階段市場「問題遠多於答案」。
財報未能撐住信心 英特爾疲弱展望加深疑慮
除了選舉後的政策風險，近期科技業財報也未能替 AI 題材建立穩固支撐。
晨星美國首席策略師 Dave Sekera 在週三發布的報告中指出，AI 類股正受到多重因素夾擊。英特爾上週公布的營收展望低於市場預期，導致股價遭到重擊，也加深投資人對資料中心建設力道可能不如原先預期的擔憂，進一步拖累輝達等其他半導體股。
Sekera 表示，市場愈來愈重視企業如何實際運用 AI 提高獲利。如果看不到相關證據，許多科技股，尤其產品具有較高商品化特性的業者，估值就可能偏高。
換言之，投資人對 AI 題材的要求正逐步提高。除了關注基礎建設支出能否持續成長，也開始檢視這些投入是否能帶來足夠的獲利回報。
多頭分析師也轉趨挑剔 資金更重視 AI 實際收益
長期看好科技股的 Yorkville Ives 分析師 Daniel Ives 也坦言，在挑選明年可能表現突出的 AI 概念股時，他與投資人都變得更加審慎。
Ives 認為，在新的政治環境下，能夠展現具體 AI 應用與投資報酬的企業，將比仰賴 AI 基礎建設擴張的晶片與記憶體業者更具優勢。
他指出，德州等關鍵州的資料中心建設，可能受到許可與監管挑戰影響，使整體 AI 建設進程「比 48 小時前看來更慢、耗時更長」。
綜合分析師觀點，這波拋售的核心，是市場開始調降對 AI 建設速度的期待，並提高對企業獲利兌現能力的要求。目前尚無法確定選後政策將使多少建設延後，但當擴張時程變得難以掌握，原本建立在快速成長預期上的晶片、記憶體與儲存設備股估值，也隨之面臨重新檢視。
paras_en: U.S. semiconductor and artificial‑intelligence (AI) concept stocks suffered a sharp sell‑off on Thursday (the 5th) as the market worries that, after the U.S. mid‑term elections, data‑center construction could face more permitting and regulatory hurdles, and that rising electricity prices are creating political pressure that may slow AI infrastructure expansion. Sandisk (SNDK‑US) tumbled 22.26%, becoming the worst‑performing component of the S&P 500; Micron (MU‑US), AMD (AMD‑US) and Western Digital (WDC‑US) each fell more than 17%.

MarketWatch reported that this wave of selling reflects investors re‑evaluating the pace of AI build‑out and the profit outlook for related companies. Analysts note that policy direction remains unclear, and recent tech earnings have failed to solidify market confidence, putting heavy pressure on chip, memory and storage stocks that rely heavily on data‑center expansion.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25% that day, its biggest single‑day drop since March 16, 2020. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, its worst day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 slid 4.36%.
At the stock level, Micron fell 17.46%, Western Digital 17.35%, AMD 17.26% and Seagate (STX‑US) 16.25%. Chip leader Nvidia (NVDA‑US) closed down 9.26%, while Intel (INTC‑US) dropped 10.33%.
Electricity prices become an election issue; the market fears data‑center expansion could be hampered
Maxim Group analyst Tom Forte said investors worry that the “tsunami‑like” mid‑term election outcome could slow the pace of data‑center expansion.

Forte pointed out that many candidates from both parties are making campaign appeals about voters’ concerns over rising electricity costs. After the election, the market will watch whether those political promises translate into measures that actually slow data‑center construction.

That means investors are currently facing the risk of possible policy changes, not a confirmed reduction in construction. How data‑center permitting, regulatory requirements and local political resistance will ultimately affect investment and build timelines remains to be clarified.
Rosenblatt Securities analyst Kevin Cassidy said it is still unclear what actions politicians will ultimately take, but “investors don’t like uncertainty.”
Jefferies trading desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza also noted that, at this stage, the market “has more questions than answers.”
Earnings fail to sustain confidence; Intel’s weak outlook deepens concerns
Beyond post‑election policy risk, recent tech earnings have also failed to provide solid support for AI‑themed stocks.

Morningstar U.S. chief strategist Dave Sekera wrote in a Wednesday report that AI‑related stocks are being hit by multiple headwinds. Intel’s revenue outlook released last week fell short of market expectations, sending its share price sharply lower and heightening investor worries that data‑center build‑out may be weaker than previously expected, which in turn drags down Nvidia and other semiconductor stocks.

Sekera said the market is increasingly focused on how companies actually use AI to boost profitability. If there is no clear evidence of that, many tech stocks—especially those whose products have higher commercialization characteristics—may be overvalued.

In other words, investors’ demands for AI‑themed companies are rising. In addition to watching whether infrastructure spending can keep growing, they are also scrutinizing whether those investments will generate sufficient profit returns.
Bullish analysts are also becoming more selective; capital is placing greater emphasis on actual AI earnings
Long‑term tech‑stock optimist Daniel Ives of Yorkville Ives admitted that, when picking AI concept stocks that could outperform next year, he and investors have become more cautious.

Ives believes that, in the new political environment, companies that can demonstrate concrete AI applications and investment returns will have an edge over chip and memory makers that rely mainly on AI infrastructure expansion.

He noted that data‑center projects in key states such as Texas could face permitting and regulatory challenges, making the overall AI build‑out “slower and more time‑consuming than it looked 48 hours ago.”

Overall analyst consensus is that the core of this sell‑off is the market’s downgrade of expectations for AI build‑out speed and a higher demand for companies to deliver profitable results. It is still uncertain how post‑election policies will delay construction, but as expansion timelines become harder to gauge, the valuations of chip, memory and storage stocks that were built on fast‑growth assumptions are now being re‑examined.

items.title: 巴克萊示警：中期選舉難救美股！AI營收與融資成本才是兩大隱憂
items.title_en: Barclays Warns Midterm Election Won’t Rescue US Stocks: AI Revenue and Financing Costs Remain Major Risks
paras: 美國投資人原本期待期中選舉結果能消除市場不確定性，為年底美股反彈行情鋪路，但巴克萊 (Barclays) (BCS-US) 警告，這場選舉恐怕無法解決當前壓制股市的核心問題。隨著市場對人工智慧 (AI) 投資回報的疑慮升高，以及資料中心與AI基礎設施建設所需的融資成本持續增加，科技股面臨的壓力可能延續至年底。
經歷10月一波艱難的市場修正後，華爾街逐漸將美國期中選舉視為股市反彈的潛在催化劑。不過，巴克萊全球股票戰術策略主管亞歷克斯·奧爾特曼 (Alex Altmann) 認為，選舉結果不太可能改變近期市場波動背後的根本因素。
奧爾特曼指出，納斯達克100指數近期下跌約10%，並不是受到期中選舉風險主導，而是市場開始擔憂AI產業的融資能力，以及相關投資究竟能否轉化為足夠的營收。他認為，選舉帶來的不確定性確實影響市場，但並非這波回檔的主要原因。
美國期中選舉結果出爐後，市場初步反應偏向正面。民主黨在國會取得重大勝利，川普也表示將接受選舉結果，美股指數期貨隨即收復先前跌幅並轉為上漲，顯示政治不確定性暫時消退，促使部分投資人逢低買進。
奧爾特曼表示，市場幾乎普遍期待期中選舉能成為短期利空出盡的契機，讓投資人重新配置資產，迎接年底傳統的聖誕老人行情 (Santa Claus Rally)，為全年交易畫下理想句點。
不過，投資人雖然先前已降低股票持倉，保留重新加碼的空間，但距離年底僅剩有限交易日，加上感恩節及聖誕節假期通常會造成市場流動性下降，可能限制年底反彈行情的持續力道。
期中選舉結果仍可能透過監管政策影響科技股，尤其是AI資料中心建設。奧爾特曼認為，選舉對AI投資交易最直接的影響，在於州政府與聯邦政府未來採取措施限制AI基礎設施建設的可能性提高。
德州就是一個重要例子。當地資料中心開發商正尋求興建數十座AI算力園區，而民主黨在此次選舉取得重大進展。民主黨籍候選人詹姆斯·塔拉里科 (James Talarico) 為民主黨取得該州自1994年以來的首個參議院席位，吉娜·伊諾霍薩 (Gina Hinojosa) 則當選州長，成為30多年來首位民主黨籍德州州長。
伊諾霍薩在競選期間多次呼籲暫停資料中心開發，這些選舉結果增加了德州收緊資料中心建設監管的可能性。奧爾特曼指出，德州在美國AI基礎設施擴張中具有關鍵地位，預計約占全美資料中心建設總量的四分之一，因此當地政策變化可能對整體AI產業造成重大影響。
然而，AI產業面臨的問題並不僅限於政治與監管。投資人目前更關注的是，科技企業投入AI基礎設施的龐大資本支出，能否帶來足夠的營收與獲利，以及企業將如何籌措資金支應這些投資。
奧爾特曼將目前股市的兩大核心驅動因素歸納為AI營收兌現能力，以及AI基礎設施建設所帶來的融資壓力。他認為，這兩項問題都不太可能在短期內獲得解決，意味著即使期中選舉暫時消除了政治不確定性，市場仍可能因AI投資回報及資金成本問題而持續震盪。
AI目前仍是一項長期投資敘事，最終能創造多少經濟價值與企業獲利，仍存在相當大的不確定性。隨著大型科技企業持續投入數千億美元建設資料中心、採購晶片及擴充運算能力，投資人開始要求更明確的營收成長證據，而不再只願意為長期成長願景支付高額估值。
奧爾特曼也質疑，市場是否過度期待期中選舉能讓短期利空一次出清。他指出，投資人普遍將這次選舉視為風險解除事件，但對AI產業而言，真正的問題並不會因選舉結束而消失。
整體而言，美國期中選舉雖然暫時緩解政治不確定性，並為美股年底行情帶來部分樂觀情緒，但AI產業的營收兌現與融資成本，才是決定科技股後續走勢的關鍵。若企業無法證明龐大AI資本支出能夠創造相應回報，或融資成本持續侵蝕獲利，即使市場迎來年底資金行情，美股仍可能面臨估值修正與波動加劇的壓力。
paras_en: US investors had hoped the midterm election results would clear market uncertainty and pave the way for a year‑end rally in US equities, but Barclays (Barclays) (BCS‑US) warns the vote is unlikely to solve the core issues suppressing the market. With growing doubts about AI investment returns and rising financing costs for data‑center and AI infrastructure construction, tech stocks may stay under pressure through year‑end.

After a tough market correction in October, Wall Street began to view the US midterms as a potential catalyst for a stock rally. However, Alex Altmann, global equity‑strategies head at Barclays, says the election outcome is unlikely to change the fundamental drivers behind recent market volatility.

Altmann notes that the Nasdaq‑100’s roughly 10% decline was not driven by midterm election risk but by market worries over AI firms’ financing ability and whether related investments can translate into sufficient revenue. He acknowledges that election‑related uncertainty does affect markets, but it is not the main cause of the pullback.

When the midterm results were announced, the market’s initial reaction was positive. Democrats secured a major win in Congress, Trump said he would accept the outcome, and US equity index futures quickly recovered their losses and turned higher, indicating a temporary easing of political uncertainty and prompting some investors to buy on dips.

Altmann says investors largely expected the midterms to serve as a short‑term “negative‑news‑out‑the‑door” event, allowing asset reallocation and setting the stage for the traditional year‑end Santa Claus rally, a desirable finish to the trading year.

Nevertheless, even though investors have trimmed equity exposure and kept room to add back, there are only a limited number of trading days left in the year. The Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays typically reduce market liquidity, which could limit the strength of any year‑end rebound.

The midterm outcome could still affect tech stocks through regulatory policy, especially AI data‑center construction. Altmann believes the most direct impact of the election on AI investment comes from a higher likelihood that state and federal governments will take steps to restrict AI infrastructure development.

Texas is a key example. Local data‑center developers are seeking to build dozens of AI compute parks, and Democrats made significant gains in this election. Democrat James Talarico won the state’s first Senate seat for the party since 1994, and Gina Hinojosa was elected governor, becoming the first Democratic governor of Texas in over three decades.

During her campaign, Hinojosa repeatedly called for a pause on data‑center development, and these election results increase the chance of tighter data‑center regulation in Texas. Altmann points out that Texas plays a critical role in US AI infrastructure expansion, accounting for roughly a quarter of the nation’s data‑center construction, so policy shifts there could have a major impact on the broader AI industry.

However, the AI sector’s challenges are not limited to politics and regulation. Investors are now more focused on whether the massive capital expenditures that tech firms are pouring into AI infrastructure will generate enough revenue and profit, and how companies will finance these investments.

Altmann boils the market’s two core drivers down to AI revenue realization and the financing pressure from AI infrastructure builds. He believes neither issue is likely to be resolved in the short term, meaning that even if the midterms temporarily remove political uncertainty, markets may continue to wobble over AI return‑on‑investment and funding‑cost concerns.

AI remains a long‑term investment narrative, with considerable uncertainty about how much economic value and corporate profit it will ultimately create. As large tech companies continue to spend hundreds of billions on data‑center construction, chip purchases and compute capacity expansion, investors are demanding clearer evidence of revenue growth rather than paying high valuations solely for a long‑term growth story.

Altmann also questions whether the market is over‑expecting the midterms to clear short‑term negatives in one go. He notes that investors broadly view the election as a risk‑removal event, but for the AI industry the real issues will not disappear simply because the vote is over.

Overall, while the US midterms have temporarily eased political uncertainty and injected some optimism into the year‑end US equity outlook, it is AI revenue realization and financing costs that will determine the future trajectory of tech stocks. If companies cannot prove that massive AI capex can generate commensurate returns, or if financing costs continue to erode profits, the market could still face valuation corrections and heightened volatility even as year‑end capital flows arrive.

items.title: 「馬斯克拋售潮」加劇！特斯拉、SpaceX兩日市值蒸發4560億美元
items.title_en: Musk Sell‑off Wave Intensifies: Tesla and SpaceX Lose $456 B in Two Days
paras: 特斯拉 (TSLA-US) 與 SpaceX (SPCX-US) 週四 (5 日) 股價雙雙重挫，美國期中選舉後的政治變局，加深市場對人工智慧 (AI) 龐大支出、資料中心建設阻力，以及馬斯克旗下企業可能面臨更嚴格國會監督的疑慮。兩家公司過去兩個交易日合計市值蒸發約 4,560 億美元，市場掀起一波「馬斯克拋售潮」。
《MarketWatch》報導，特斯拉週四收跌 10.77%，SpaceX 下挫 9.05%。據道瓊市場數據，特斯拉兩日市值縮水約 2,160 億美元，SpaceX 則減少約 2,400 億美元。
《富比士》估計，馬斯克身家當天下降約 9%，至 7,895 億美元。
這波跌勢同時反映科技股整體賣壓，以及投資人對馬斯克企業版圖政治風險的重新評估。分析師指出，民主黨奪回參眾兩院控制權後，資料中心擴張、政府合約與特斯拉和 SpaceX 潛在合併案，都可能面臨更多變數。
AI 支出疑慮升溫 德州政治變局增添建設風險
CFRA 分析師尼爾森 (Garrett Nelson) 表示，民主黨拿下國會兩院，進一步加深投資人對特斯拉及其他大型科技公司龐大 AI 支出計畫的憂慮。
尼爾森指出，對於在德州等民主黨此次取得重大勝利的州經營業務的企業，市場疑慮尤其明顯。特斯拉與 SpaceX 總部均位於德州，特斯拉也在當地營運超級運算叢集；SpaceX 的資料中心則位於密西西比州與田納西州。
包括德州候任州長希諾霍薩 (Gina Hinojosa) 在內，多名新當選民主黨人士曾表態反對新建資料中心。顧問公司 Redbud Consulting 指出，本週交由選民表決的資料中心相關提案有數十項，截至該公司統計時，資料中心支持陣營僅贏得其中一項。
這使市場擔心，AI 投資即使持續增加，實際建設仍可能因地方政治、許可及監管程序而延後，拉長資金投入轉化為營收與獲利的時間。
不過，民主黨人士對馬斯克企業的態度並非全然負面。德州候任聯邦參議員塔拉里科 (James Talarico) 最近接受 NBC 訪問時表示，自己是 SpaceX 與特斯拉的「忠實支持者」，願意與馬斯克合作推動德州科技創新，儘管馬斯克先前支持的是他的共和黨對手。
馬斯克週四在社群平台 X 回應：「他這麼說很友善。」
地面建設阻力增加 太空資料中心構想受關注
KeyBanc 分析師 Mike Leshock 認為，政治阻力可能促使 SpaceX 加快將資料中心部署至軌道的腳步，而這項目標對公司未來發展及估值具有關鍵意義。
馬斯克週三也在 X 發文表示，太空資料中心「現在看起來相當有吸引力」。
不過，地面建設可能受阻的疑慮，已先衝擊整體 AI 基礎建設供應鏈。Globalt Investments 投資組合經理馬丁 (Thomas Martin) 指出，週四賣壓特別集中於可能受到美國資料中心建設放緩影響的企業，戴爾 (DELL-US) 與希捷 (STX-US) 即是其中代表。
戴爾週四下跌 14.70%，希捷下挫 16.25%；輝達 (NVDA-US) 重挫 9.26%，單日市值蒸發約 4,470 億美元，創公司史上第二大單日市值損失。Sandisk (SNDK-US) 則暴跌 22.26%，為標普 500 指數表現最差成分股。
那斯達克 100 指數下跌 6.36%，費城半導體指數下挫 12.25%，雙雙創下 2020 年 3 月 16 日以來最大單日跌幅。
政治關係成估值變數 國會監督風險上升
除了資料中心前景，投資人也開始重新衡量，馬斯克與川普及共和黨的緊密關係，可能為旗下企業帶來哪些風險。
Direxion 資本市場主管 Jake Behan 表示，這波「馬斯克拋售潮」，反映市場正在重新評估投資價值高度繫於單一人物所帶來的風險。如今，投資人必須在明顯較不友善的政治環境下，重新檢視 SpaceX 與特斯拉的前景。
SpaceX 是美國政府的重要承包商，曾領導「政府效率部」的馬斯克也正與國防部合作。報導指出，多名民主黨國會議員已在準備針對馬斯克展開調查。
根據政治獻金追蹤機構 OpenSecrets，馬斯克是 2026 年選舉週期最大的個人捐款者，投入約 4.457 億美元，多數資金用於支持共和黨候選人。
隨著國會控制權易手，這些政治連結也成為投資人評估企業監督與政策風險的重要因素。
特斯拉、SpaceX 潛在合併案 面臨更複雜審查環境
市場另一項關注焦點，是特斯拉與 SpaceX 正在進行的初步合併磋商。
若交易成形，馬斯克旗下兩大企業將整合至同一家公司，並可能由他高度掌控，形成外界所稱的「馬斯克企業帝國」(Elon, Inc.)。
不過，這類整合可能引發美國監管機關與國會議員關切，選後政治環境也可能增加交易推進的難度。
Aptus Capital Advisors 投資組合經理 David Wagner 表示，更大的問題在於特斯拉與 SpaceX 擬議中的合併。他指出，一個對馬斯克較不友善的國會，將使這條路變得更加複雜，儘管這不代表國會就能自動阻止交易。
從分析師觀點來看，兩家公司目前承受的是多重風險疊加：科技股整體估值承壓、AI 建設時程可能拉長，加上國會監督及潛在合併審查的不確定性。政治變局是否實際影響企業投資、政府業務與整合計畫，將成為市場後續觀察重點。
paras_en: Tesla (TSLA-US) and SpaceX (SPCX-US) saw their shares plunge on Thursday (the 5th), as post‑midterm election political shifts in the United States deepened market concerns about massive AI spending, data‑center construction hurdles, and the possibility of stricter congressional oversight of Musk’s companies. Over the past two trading days the two firms together erased about $456 billion in market value, sparking a wave of what analysts call a “Musk sell‑off.”

MarketWatch reported that Tesla closed down 10.77% on Thursday while SpaceX fell 9.05%. According to Dow Jones market data, Tesla’s market cap shrank by roughly $216 billion over the two days, and SpaceX’s by about $240 billion.
Forbes estimated that Musk’s net worth dropped about 9% that day, to $789.5 billion.

The decline also mirrors broader selling pressure in tech stocks and a reassessment by investors of the political risks surrounding Musk’s corporate empire. Analysts note that after Democrats regain control of both chambers of Congress, data‑center expansion, government contracts and potential Tesla‑SpaceX merger deals could face additional variables.
AI‑spending worries heat up as Texas political shifts add construction risk
CFRA analyst Garrett Nelson said that a Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress deepens investor anxiety over the huge AI‑spending plans of Tesla and other large tech firms.

Nelson pointed out that companies operating in states where Democrats have just won major victories—such as Texas, where both Tesla and SpaceX are headquartered—face especially pronounced market concerns. Tesla runs a super‑computing cluster in Texas; SpaceX’s data centers are located in Mississippi and Tennessee.

Several newly elected Democrats, including Texas lieutenant‑governor‑elect Gina Hinojosa, have voiced opposition to new data‑center projects. Redbud Consulting noted that dozens of data‑center proposals were on the ballot this week, and the pro‑data‑center side won only one of them according to the firm’s tally.

This has led the market to worry that even if AI investment continues to rise, actual construction could be delayed by local politics, permitting and regulatory processes, lengthening the time it takes for capital to turn into revenue and profit.

However, Democratic attitudes toward Musk’s companies are not uniformly negative. Texas Senate candidate James Talarico told NBC that he is a “loyal supporter” of SpaceX and Tesla and is willing to work with Musk to promote tech innovation in Texas, even though Musk previously backed his Republican opponent.
Musk replied on X on Thursday: “He’s being very friendly.”
Ground‑construction resistance rises as space‑based data‑center concepts draw attention

KeyBanc analyst Mike Leshock believes political resistance could push SpaceX to accelerate plans to deploy data centers in orbit, a goal he sees as critical to the company’s future growth and valuation.
Musk also posted on X on Wednesday that a space‑based data center “now looks quite attractive.”

Nevertheless, concerns that ground construction could be hampered have already hit the broader AI infrastructure supply chain. Thomas Martin, portfolio manager at Globalt Investments, said Thursday’s selling pressure was concentrated in firms that could be affected by a slowdown in U.S. data‑center builds, with Dell (DELL-US) and Seagate (STX-US) as prime examples.

Dell fell 14.70% on Thursday, Seagate dropped 16.25%; Nvidia (NVDA-US) plunged 9.26%, wiping out about $447 billion in market value in a single day—the second‑largest one‑day loss in the company’s history. Sandisk (SNDK-US) tumbled 22.26%, making it the worst‑performing component of the S&P 500.
The Nasdaq‑100 slid 6.36% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.25%, each marking their biggest single‑day declines since March 16, 2020.
Political ties become valuation variables as congressional oversight risk rises
Beyond data‑center outlooks, investors are re‑evaluating how Musk’s close relationship with Trump and the Republican Party could pose risks to his businesses.

Direxion capital markets head Jake Behan said the current “Musk sell‑off” reflects the market’s reassessment of the risk of having investment value so tightly linked to a single individual. In a now less‑friendly political environment, investors must re‑examine the prospects for SpaceX and Tesla.

SpaceX is a major U.S. government contractor; Musk, who once led the Department of Government Efficiency, is also working with the Defense Department. Reports indicate that several Democratic members of Congress are preparing investigations into Musk.

According to political‑donation tracker OpenSecrets, Musk is the largest individual donor in the 2026 election cycle, contributing roughly $445.7 million, most of which supports Republican candidates.
As congressional control shifts, these political connections become an important factor for investors assessing corporate oversight and policy risk.
Tesla and SpaceX’s potential merger faces a more complex review environment
Another market focus is the early‑stage merger talks between Tesla and SpaceX.
If the deal materialises, Musk’s two flagship companies would be combined into a single entity, potentially under his tight control, creating what outsiders refer to as the “Elon, Inc.” empire.
However, such integration could trigger concerns from U.S. regulators and members of Congress, and the post‑election political climate could make advancing the transaction more difficult.

Aptus Capital Advisors portfolio manager David Wagner said the bigger issue is the proposed Tesla‑SpaceX merger. He noted that a Congress less friendly to Musk would make the path considerably more complicated, though it does not automatically mean Congress could block the deal.

Analysts view the two companies as currently bearing multiple overlapping risks: pressure on overall tech‑stock valuations, possible lengthening of AI‑infrastructure timelines, and uncertainty from congressional oversight and potential merger scrutiny. Whether the political upheaval will materially affect corporate investment, government business and integration plans will be a key focus for the market going forward.

items.title_en: Baron Analysis: Micron Plummets Over 17%! Buying Opportunity Emerging or Downtrend Not Over?
paras: 美光 (MU-US) 週四 (5 日) 重挫 17.46%，市場擔憂資料中心建設可能放緩，加上記憶體供給過剩疑慮，引發相關類股全面下殺。不過，儘管美光第三季在全球動態隨機存取記憶體 (DRAM) 市場的市占率下滑，整體市場規模仍大幅擴張，尚不能單憑市占率變化，就認定其業務前景轉弱。
《巴隆週刊》報導，民主黨在期中選舉勝出後，投資人擔心，資料中心開發案可能面臨更多阻力，拖慢建設進度，進而影響記憶體與儲存設備需求。
美光 (MU-US) 週四暴跌 17.46%，下跌 138.84 美元，收在 656.39 美元，延續前一交易日約 7% 的跌勢。相較於 6 月 25 日創下的 1,213.56 美元收盤高點，股價已回落約 45.9%。
其他記憶體與儲存設備類股同步重挫。SanDisk (SNDK-US) 暴跌 22.26%，收在 806.43 美元；威騰 (WDC-US) 重挫 17.35%，收在 267.63 美元；希捷 (STX-US) 下跌 16.25%，收在 466.53 美元；SK 海力士ADR (SKHY-US) 下挫 13.40%，收在 123.90 美元。
美光與同業的產品是資料中心的重要零組件，其中 DRAM 為處理器提供高速工作記憶體，NAND 快閃記憶體與硬碟則用於儲存資料。因此，一旦資料中心投資放緩，相關業者的成長預期也可能受到衝擊。
AI 支出疑慮升溫，市場憂心供需失衡
市場對記憶體產業的擔憂並非始於選舉。
兩週前，美光就曾單日下殺逾 6%，當時投資人已開始質疑 Meta、亞馬遜等大型雲端業者能否持續投入龐大 AI 支出，以及為擴張而增加的債務是否帶來財務壓力。
如今，資料中心建設可能放緩的疑慮，又加深市場對未來供需失衡的擔心。若需求成長不如預期，先前因應 AI 熱潮而增加的供給，可能成為壓抑價格的因素。
市占率下滑，但 DRAM 營收仍大幅成長
在這樣的背景下，美光第三季 DRAM 市占率由去年同期的 26% 降至 21%，乍看之下似乎又是一項利空。DRAM 約占美光總營收四分之三，因此這項業務的表現格外受到關注。
不過，市占率下降並不代表營收萎縮。
根據 Counterpoint Research 數據，受平均售價上漲帶動，第三季全球 DRAM 市場營收年增 369%，約為去年同期的 4.7 倍。美光的 DRAM 營收也大幅成長，只是增速落後三星與 SK 海力士，使其市占率下滑。
Counterpoint Research 資深分析師Jeongku Choi指出，這波行情主要由價格上漲推動，而非出貨量大幅增加。當季 DRAM 位元出貨量僅成長約 4%，市場營收卻逼近 2,000 億美元，顯示價格是推升營收的主要動力。
他認為，AI 已讓記憶體從一般大宗商品，轉變為供應吃緊的關鍵資源，買方的重點也從議價轉向確保供貨。
此外，中國記憶體業者長鑫存儲 (CXMT) 第三季市占率由第二季的 10% 降至 9%，可能稍微緩解投資人對中國業者持續搶占市場的疑慮。
整體而言，美光股價反映的是市場對未來 AI 支出與記憶體供需的擔憂，目前的產業數據則顯示，DRAM 市場營收仍在快速成長。市占率下滑值得留意，但尚不足以單獨證明美光的成長動能已經逆轉。
paras_en: Micron (MU-US) slumped 17.46% on Thursday (the 5th) as the market worries that data‑center construction could slow, compounded by concerns over excess memory supply, triggering a broad sell‑off in related stocks. However, despite Micron's third‑quarter share‑price decline in the global DRAM market, the overall market size is still expanding sharply, so a change in market share alone does not prove a weakening business outlook.

Baron Weekly reported that after Democrats won the mid‑term elections, investors fear data‑center projects may face more resistance, slowing construction progress and consequently dampening demand for memory and storage devices.

Micron (MU-US) tumbled 17.46% on Thursday, down $138.84 to close at $656.39, extending the roughly 7% drop from the previous trading day. Compared with the June 25 peak close of $1,213.56, the price has fallen about 45.9%.

Other memory and storage stocks fell in tandem. SanDisk (SNDK-US) plunged 22.26% to $806.43; Western Digital (WDC‑US) slid 17.35% to $267.63; Seagate (STX‑US) dropped 16.25% to $466.53; SK Hynix ADR (SKHY‑US) fell 13.40% to $123.90.

Micron’s products, like those of its peers, are key components for data centers, with DRAM providing high‑speed working memory for processors and NAND flash and hard drives used for data storage. Thus, a slowdown in data‑center investment could hit growth expectations for these companies.
AI‑spending concerns are heating up, and the market worries about a supply‑demand imbalance.
Market worries about the memory industry did not start with the election.

Two weeks ago, Micron had already dropped more than 6% in a single day, when investors began questioning whether large cloud players such as Meta and Amazon could continue to pour massive AI spending and whether the debt taken on for expansion would create financial pressure.

Now, doubts that data‑center construction may slow deepen market concerns about a future supply‑demand mismatch. If demand growth falls short of expectations, the extra supply added to ride the AI wave could become a price‑pressuring factor.
Share‑price decline but DRAM revenue still growing sharply

In this context, Micron’s third‑quarter DRAM market share fell from 26% a year ago to 21%, which at first glance appears another negative. DRAM accounts for about three‑quarters of Micron’s total revenue, so this segment draws particular attention.
However, a lower market share does not necessarily mean shrinking revenue.

According to Counterpoint Research, rising average selling prices drove global DRAM market revenue up 369% year‑over‑year in Q3, roughly 4.7 times the level a year earlier. Micron’s DRAM revenue also grew markedly, but its growth lagged Samsung and SK Hynix, causing its share to slip.

Counterpoint senior analyst Jeongku Choi said the rally was driven mainly by price increases rather than a sharp rise in shipment volumes. DRAM bit shipments grew only about 4% that quarter, while market revenue approached $200 billion, showing price as the main revenue driver.
He believes AI has turned memory from a generic commodity into a tightly‑sourced critical resource, shifting buyers’ focus from price negotiation to securing supply.
In addition, Chinese memory maker CXMT’s Q3 market share fell from 10% in Q2 to 9%, which may slightly ease investor concerns about Chinese firms continuously grabbing market share.

Overall, Micron’s stock reflects market anxiety over future AI spending and memory supply‑demand dynamics, while industry data show DRAM market revenue is still growing rapidly. The share‑price decline in market share warrants attention but is not enough on its own to prove Micron’s growth momentum has reversed.

paras: 美股週四 (5 日) 遭遇全面拋售，市場擔憂民主黨在期中選舉大勝後，將加強人工智慧 (AI) 與資料中心監管，引爆晶片及 AI 基礎建設類股賣壓。道瓊狂瀉逾 1,833 點，回吐前一日選後漲幅；那斯達克指數暴跌 5.52%，跌入修正區間，費城半導體指數更下殺 12.25%，創 2020 年 3 月 16 日以來最大單日跌幅。
美股三大指數均創下 2025 年 4 月以來最差單日表現。那斯達克 100 指數下跌約 6.4%，創 2020 年 3 月以來最大單日跌幅，單日市值蒸發約 2.3 兆美元。小型股羅素 2000 指數也下挫 4.45%，與那指雙雙較近期高點回落逾 10%，進入修正區間。
民主黨奪下國會參眾兩院，並在關鍵州長選舉勝出後，投資人開始重新評估 AI 資料中心的建設速度，以及相關企業龐大資本支出的回收前景。
與民主黨保持著密切聯繫參議員桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 呼籲全國暫停興建資料中心，進一步加深市場對監管收緊的疑慮。不過，相關主張目前仍屬政治倡議，尚不代表全國性禁令已經實施。
Meta 總裁暨副董事長 Dina Powell McCormick 週三出席《華爾街日報》科技論壇時，也坦言選後興建資料中心將變得「更加困難」。但她同時提到，一名勝選州長已表達希望保留當地投資與就業機會，顯示地方政府仍須在民意壓力與經濟利益之間取得平衡。
市場原先期待選舉結果明朗，有助降低政治不確定性，帶動週三道瓊大漲逾 1,500 點。然而，隨著焦點轉向 AI 投資與企業獲利風險，週四賣壓迅速由科技股向其他產業擴散。
資金轉向美債避險，10 年期美債殖利率下滑約 6 個基點至 4.83%。比特幣下滑約 5.4%，至 75,809.84 美元，西德州原油漲超 2%至每桶 90.54 美元，現貨黃金升至約每盎司 4,082.01 美元。
投資人接下來將關注週五公布的美國 10 月非農就業報告，觀察勞動市場與利率前景，但 AI 投資能否維持成長，仍是左右科技股信心的關鍵。

企業新聞
投資人憂慮AI監管趨嚴，使資料中心建設、伺服器與記憶體採購遞延，拖累記憶體及儲存族群，美光 (MU-US) 下殺 17.46% 至每股 656.39 美元。此外，美光因長期勞資爭議，暫停一項約 45 億美元的台灣記憶體廠計畫，增添擴產不確定性。
AI巨頭輝達亦首當其衝，輝達 (NVDA-US) 重摔 9.26% 至 181.60 美元，市值單日蒸發4,470億美元。

SanDisk (SNDK-US) 狂瀉 22.26% 至每股 806.43 美元。該公司原本是 AI 投資熱潮的代表性個股之一，但民主黨「藍潮」席捲國會後，股價遭到拋售。

高通 (QCOM-US) 重摔 9.49% 至每股 156.75 美元。這家晶片商公布的第四財季營收優於預期，但警告晶片設計部門接下來的利潤率將走弱，打擊投資人信心。
安謀 (Arm)(ARM-US) 慘跌超13% 至每股 166.72 美元。這家英國晶片架構設計商第二財季獲利表現穩健，但記憶體價格飆升衝擊智慧手機市場，導致權利金收入疲弱，蓋過財報亮點。
華爾街分析
JonesTrading 分析師 Michael O’Rourke 認為，政治版圖改變將使資料中心建設實際放緩，原先支撐科技股估值的獲利預期也須重新評估。由於投資人尚不清楚獲利預估將下修至何種程度，因此選擇先降低風險曝險。
OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners 投資長 Peter Boockvar 表示，AI 技術本身仍將持續發展，但如果資料中心、建築與相關基礎設施的實際建設速度放慢，股價就會反映這項變化。
Northlight Asset Management 投資長 Chris Zaccarelli 則認為，市場反應過於極端。他同意資料中心建設將面臨更多阻力，但強調，只要專案具備商業效益，仍有機會推動。
Truist Wealth 投資長 Keith Lerner 指出，科技股跌勢的規模已開始衝擊整體市場。隨著拋售擴散，短期市場走勢將更取決於投資人何時願意重新承擔風險。

paras_en: US stocks on Thursday (the 5th) faced a broad sell‑off as markets worried that a Democratic landslide in the midterm elections would tighten regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers, sparking selling pressure on chip and AI‑infrastructure stocks. The Dow plunged more than 1,833 points, erasing the post‑election gains of the previous day; the Nasdaq fell 5.52%, slipping into correction territory, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tumbled 12.25%, its biggest single‑day drop since March 16, 2020.

All three major US indices posted their worst single‑day performance since April 2025. The Nasdaq‑100 fell about 6.4%, the steepest one‑day decline since March 2020, wiping out roughly $2.3 trillion in market value. The Russell 2000 small‑cap index also dropped 4.45%, with both it and the Nasdaq falling more than 10% from recent highs and entering correction zones.

After Democrats secured control of both houses of Congress and won key gubernatorial races, investors began reassessing the pace of AI data‑center construction and the outlook for recouping the massive capital expenditures of related companies.

Senator Bernie Sanders, who maintains close ties with the Democratic Party, called for a nationwide pause on building new data centers, deepening market concerns about tighter regulation. However, the proposal remains a political initiative and does not constitute a nationwide ban.

Meta’s president and vice‑chair Dina Powell McCormick told the Wall Street Journal’s tech forum on Wednesday that post‑election data‑center construction would become “even more difficult.” She added that a winning governor has expressed a desire to preserve local investment and jobs, indicating that state officials must balance public pressure with economic interests.

The market had initially hoped that a clear election outcome would reduce political uncertainty, helping the Dow surge more than 1,500 points on Wednesday. As focus shifted to AI investment and corporate profit risks, Thursday’s selling pressure quickly spread from tech stocks to other sectors.

Funds fled to US Treasury safe‑haven assets, with the 10‑year Treasury yield slipping about six basis points to 4.83%. Bitcoin fell roughly 5.4% to $75,809.84, West Texas Intermediate crude rose more than 2% to $90.54 per barrel, and spot gold climbed to about $4,082.01 per ounce.

Investors will now watch Friday’s US October non‑farm payroll report for clues on the labor market and interest‑rate outlook, but whether AI investment can sustain growth remains the key factor influencing tech‑stock confidence.
US stock index performance on Thursday (the 5th):

The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,833.06 points, or 3.44%, to 51,523.06. The Nasdaq fell 1,421.52 points, or 5.52%, to 24,315.00. The S&P 500 dropped 334.89 points, or 4.36%, to 7,353.73. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 1,257.52 points, or 12.25%, to 9,011.14. The NYSE FANG+ Index slid 1,066.96 points, or 6.00%, to 16,718.26.

Key stocks:
The five big‑tech names in the NYSE FANG+ Index all moved lower. Meta (META‑US) fell 3.96%; Apple (AAPL‑US) dropped 1.53%; Alphabet (GOOGL‑US) slipped 2.20%; Microsoft (MSFT‑US) declined 3.58%; Amazon (AMZN‑US) lost 2.19%.

The Philadelphia semiconductor sector faced heavy selling. AMD (AMD‑US) plunged 17.26%; Broadcom (AVGO‑US) fell 10.43%; Nvidia (NVDA‑US) dropped 9.26%; Applied Materials (AMAT‑US) slid 13.58%; Qualcomm (QCOM‑US) fell 9.49%.

Memory and storage stocks were drenched in red. Micron (MU‑US) tumbled 17.46%; Western Digital (WDC‑US) fell 17.35%; SanDisk (SNDK‑US) crashed 22.26%; Seagate (STX‑US) dropped 16.25%; SK Hynix ADR (SKHY‑US) slid 13.40%.
Taiwan‑related ADRs were hammered. TSMC ADR (TSM‑US) fell 10.78%; ASE Technology ADR (ASX‑US) plunged 20.77%; UMC ADR (UMC‑US) dropped 16.69%; Chunghwa Telecom ADR (CHT‑US) slipped 0.24%.
Corporate news:

Investors worry that tighter AI regulation will delay data‑center builds and the procurement of servers and memory, hurting memory and storage groups. Micron (MU‑US) fell 17.46% to $656.39 per share. In addition, Micron paused a roughly $4.5 billion Taiwan memory‑fab project amid a long‑standing labor dispute, adding uncertainty to its expansion plans.
AI leader Nvidia was also hit hard, sliding 9.26% to $181.60, wiping out $447 billion of market value in a single day.

Intel (INTC‑US) fell 10.33% to $52.25 as weak forecasts, supply constraints and a sluggish PC business weighed on the stock, with the one‑month decline potentially expanding beyond 55%. AMD (AMD‑US) simultaneously plunged more than 17%.
SanDisk (SNDK‑US) crashed 22.26% to $806.43 per share. The company had been a flagship AI‑investment play, but after the Democratic “blue wave” swept Congress, the stock was sold off.
Data‑center power and cooling equipment supplier Vertiv (VRT‑US) plunged 14.02% to $176.73 per share as investors withdrew from AI‑themed stocks, raising concerns about its business outlook.

Bloom Energy (BE‑US) sank 16.41% to $167.52 per share, though the drop may be an overreaction; CEO KR Sridhar has said that a rebound in data‑center demand could actually create opportunities for the company.
Palantir (PLTR‑US) fell 9.73% to $154.99, its biggest single‑day decline since February 4, even though the firm recently reported third‑quarter earnings that beat expectations.

Qualcomm (QCOM‑US) dropped 9.49% to $156.75. The chipmaker posted fourth‑quarter revenue ahead of forecasts but warned that profit margins in its chip‑design division would weaken, denting investor confidence.

Arm (ARM‑US) tumbled more than 13% to $166.72. The UK‑based chip‑architecture designer posted solid second‑quarter earnings, but soaring memory prices hurt the smartphone market, weakening royalty revenue and offsetting the positive earnings news.
Wall Street analysis:

JonesTrading analyst Michael O’Rourke believes the shifting political landscape will slow data‑center construction, forcing a reassessment of the profit expectations that have underpinned tech‑stock valuations. Because investors are unsure how far earnings forecasts will be cut, they are opting to reduce risk exposure.

Peter Boockvar, CIO of OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners, says AI technology will continue to evolve, but if the pace of building data‑centers, buildings and related infrastructure slows, stock prices will reflect that change.

Chris Zaccarelli, CIO of Northlight Asset Management, thinks the market reaction is overly extreme. He agrees data‑center construction will face more headwinds but stresses that projects with clear commercial benefits can still move forward.

Keith Lerner, CIO of Truist Wealth, notes that the scale of the tech‑stock decline is beginning to affect the broader market. As the sell‑off spreads, short‑term market direction will depend more on when investors are willing to take on risk again.

items.title: 〈能源盤後〉美伊和談仍卡關 油輪遇襲頻傳！原油自前一日深跌反彈
items.title_en: Energy After-Hours: US‑Iran Talks Still Stalled, Tanker Attacks Frequent; Crude Rebounds After Yesterday’s Deep Drop
paras: 中東油輪遇襲事件再度引發市場對原油供應中斷的憂慮，國際油價周四 (5日) 強勢反彈，布蘭特原油 (Brent) 期貨收盤大漲3.67美元，漲幅3.88%，報每桶98.29美元；美國西德州中級原油 (WTI) 期貨上漲2.40美元，漲幅2.72%，收在每桶90.52美元，扭轉前一交易日雙雙重挫逾8%的走勢。
周三 (4日) 油價大幅下跌，兩大原油期貨指標均跌至8月31日以來最低收盤水準，主要受到美國期中選舉結果改變市場對伊朗戰爭走向的預期影響。然而，隨著波斯灣油輪遇襲事件接連發生，加上美伊外交談判仍缺乏實質進展，市場開始重新評估原油供應能否迅速恢復正常，促使油價反彈。
市場分析指出，此次油價回升反映投資人對原油運輸迅速恢復正常抱持審慎態度。在外交進展尚未真正轉化為穩定的船舶運輸與實際交貨之前，市場仍難以完全排除供應中斷風險。Lipow Oil Associates總裁安迪·利波 (Andy Lipow) 指出，市場持續擔憂中東油輪可能觸及水雷，或遭無人機攻擊，而伊朗對美國談判的立場也沒有出現明顯改變。
英國海事貿易行動辦公室 (UKMTO) 表示，自周日以來，至少已有5艘船舶通報遭遇相關事件，波斯灣油輪遇襲頻率仍接近戰爭爆發以來的高點。10月共有35艘船舶通報遭遇攻擊或相關事件，創下這場戰爭期間單月最高紀錄。近期事件頻率與10月高峰相近，顯示即使市場一度押注中東衝突降溫，能源運輸安全仍未獲得保障。
伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊表示，有兩艘油輪及一艘拖船因試圖使用未經授權的荷姆茲海峽航線，在不同事件中起火。荷姆茲海峽是全球最重要的能源運輸通道之一，任何船舶遇襲、航線受阻或保險成本上升，都可能影響波斯灣原油出口，進一步推升國際能源市場的風險溢價。
美國與以色列自2月對伊朗發動戰爭以來，能源價格大幅上漲，燃料成本也成為美國選民不滿的重要因素。周二 (3日) 美國期中選舉結果出爐，民主黨取得國會參眾兩院控制權，擊敗川普所屬的共和黨。新一屆由民主黨掌控的國會將於明年1月正式就任。
選舉結果一度讓市場預期，民主黨可能加大對白宮的政治壓力，促使川普政府尋求結束伊朗戰爭，降低中東局勢對能源價格及美國民生物價的衝擊。不過，花旗集團 (Citigroup) 指出，期中選舉結束後，白宮可能轉而運用行政部門在外交政策上的權力，甚至進一步升高對伊朗的軍事行動，反而讓市場對衝突升級保持警惕。
地緣政治研究機構歐亞集團 (Eurasia Group) 則調整對美伊戰爭後續發展的預測。該機構將美國再次對伊朗發動攻擊的機率，從原先的65%下調至60%；美伊達成外交協議的機率，則從20%降至10%。相較之下，雙方持續陷入長期對峙的機率，從15%大幅提高至30%。
伊朗目前仍堅持其談判條件，而川普被認為不太可能接受相關要求，使外交突破的難度增加。歐亞集團警告，儘管近期油價從高點回落，但若中東衝突再次升級，布蘭特原油可能重新升至每桶110至125美元區間，顯示市場目前的價格仍未完全反映最嚴重的供應風險。
外交方面，伊朗外交部長阿拉格齊 (Abbas Araqchi) 分別與沙烏地阿拉伯及卡達外長通話，討論促進區域穩定的外交努力最新進展。不過，相關接觸尚未代表美伊談判取得突破，區域安全局勢依舊緊張。
沙烏地阿拉伯周四也針對紅海沿岸重要石油出口樞紐延布 (Yanbu) 發出潛在危險警報。與伊朗立場接近的葉門胡塞武裝持續對沙烏地阿拉伯發動攻擊，讓戰事風險進一步擴大至紅海沿岸。胡塞武裝隨後聲稱攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯達曼市的法赫德國王機場，但沙烏地官方當時並未立即證實相關說法。
除了中東局勢，俄羅斯能源基礎設施也面臨新的攻擊風險。烏克蘭重新加強對俄羅斯煉油廠的無人機攻擊，引發市場對俄羅斯柴油出口能力的擔憂。根據《路透社》對影像的分析，俄羅斯梁贊煉油廠疑似在莫斯科東南方一處工業區的大規模夜間無人機攻擊中遭到打擊。若消息獲得確認，這將是俄羅斯本周第二座遭到攻擊的煉油廠，此前雅羅斯拉夫爾煉油廠已於周一晚間遇襲。
俄羅斯柴油出口能力受到關注，也與美俄能源供應安排及川普政府相關協議有關。若煉油設施持續遭到破壞，可能進一步影響俄羅斯成品油出口，為全球柴油市場帶來額外不確定性。
整體而言，周四油價反彈凸顯能源市場目前仍處於高度矛盾的局面。一方面，美國期中選舉結果帶來戰爭降溫的期待，促使投資人降低部分地緣政治風險溢價；另一方面，油輪遇襲、荷姆茲海峽航運安全、胡塞武裝攻擊及俄羅斯煉油設施受損，都顯示全球能源供應鏈尚未恢復穩定。
短期油價走勢將取決於美伊外交能否取得實質進展，以及中東主要航運路線是否恢復安全。若戰事持續、油輪攻擊頻率維持高檔，或原油出口受到進一步限制，油價可能重新累積上行壓力；反之，若外交談判取得突破且能源運輸逐步恢復，先前累積的地緣政治風險溢價則可能再次消退。
paras_en: Middle‑East tanker attacks reignited market worries about crude supply disruptions, sending international oil prices sharply higher on Thursday (the 5th). Brent futures closed up $3.67, a 3.88% gain, at $98.29 a barrel; U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose $2.40, or 2.72%, to $90.52, reversing the double‑digit losses of more than 8% seen the previous session.

On Wednesday (the 4th) oil prices plunged, with both major crude futures sinking to their lowest close since Aug. 31, driven mainly by U.S. mid‑term election results that altered market expectations about the direction of the Iran war. However, a spate of attacks on Gulf tankers and the lack of substantive progress in U.S.–Iran diplomatic talks prompted a reassessment of how quickly oil supply could normalize, pushing prices back up.

Analysts said the rebound reflects investors’ cautious optimism that oil transport will quickly return to normal. Until diplomatic gains translate into stable shipping and actual deliveries, the market cannot fully rule out supply‑interruption risk. Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates, noted continued concerns that Middle‑East tankers could hit mines or be hit by drones, and that Iran’s negotiating stance toward the U.S. has not shifted noticeably.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that since Sunday at least five vessels have reported related incidents, with the frequency of Gulf tanker attacks still near the peak seen since the war began. In October, 35 vessels reported attacks or related events, the highest monthly total during the conflict. The recent pace is comparable to that October high, showing that even when markets once bet on a cooling of Middle‑East fighting, energy‑transport security remains unguaranteed.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire while attempting to use an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz in separate incidents. The Hormuz Strait is one of the world’s most vital energy corridors, and any vessel attacks, route blockages or rising insurance costs could affect Gulf crude exports and lift the risk premium in global energy markets.

U.S. and Israeli war‑on‑Iran actions since February have driven energy prices sharply higher, making fuel costs a major source of voter discontent in the United States. On Tuesday (the 3rd) the mid‑term election results were announced, giving Democrats control of both chambers of Congress and defeating the Republican Party of former President Trump. The new Democratic‑led Congress will take office in January next year.

The election initially led markets to expect that Democrats might increase political pressure on the White House, prompting the Trump administration to seek an end to the Iran war and lower the impact of Middle‑East tensions on energy prices and U.S. consumer inflation. However, Citigroup warned that after the mid‑terms the White House could instead use executive authority on foreign policy to heighten military actions against Iran, keeping the market wary of an escalation.

Geopolitical‑risk firm Eurasia Group revised its outlook for the U.S.–Iran conflict. It lowered the probability of a U.S. renewed attack on Iran from 65% to 60% and cut the chance of a diplomatic agreement from 20% to 10%. Conversely, the likelihood of a prolonged stalemate rose sharply from 15% to 30%.

Iran still insists on its negotiating terms, and Trump is seen as unlikely to accept them, making a diplomatic breakthrough harder. Eurasia Group warned that although oil prices have retreated from recent highs, a renewed escalation in the Middle East could push Brent back into the $110‑$125 a barrel range, indicating that current prices do not fully reflect the worst‑case supply risk.

Diplomatically, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi held separate calls with the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Qatar to discuss the latest diplomatic efforts to promote regional stability. Yet these contacts have not signaled a breakthrough in U.S.–Iran talks, and regional security remains tense.

Saudi Arabia on Thursday also issued a potential danger alert for the key Red Sea oil‑export hub of Yanbu. Yemen’s Houthi forces, aligned with Iran, continue attacks on Saudi Arabia, expanding war risk to the Red Sea coast. The Houthis later claimed an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, though Saudi officials did not immediately confirm the report.

Beyond the Middle East, Russia’s energy infrastructure faces new attack risks. Ukraine has stepped up drone strikes on Russian refineries, sparking market worries about Russia’s diesel export capacity. Reuters analysis of footage suggests the Liuzhou refinery may have been hit in a large‑scale night‑time drone raid in an industrial area southeast of Moscow. If confirmed, this would be Russia’s second refinery hit this week, following an attack on the Yaroslavl plant on Monday night.

Russia’s diesel export capability is under scrutiny, also because of U.S.–Russia energy‑supply arrangements and agreements linked to the Trump administration. Continued damage to refining assets could further curb Russian product‑oil exports, adding extra uncertainty to the global diesel market.

Overall, Thursday’s price rebound highlights the energy market’s contradictory state. On one hand, the U.S. mid‑term results raised hopes of a war de‑escalation, prompting investors to trim some geopolitical risk premiums; on the other hand, tanker attacks, Hormuz shipping safety concerns, Houthi strikes and damage to Russian refineries all show that the global energy supply chain has not yet stabilized.

In the short term, oil‑price direction will hinge on whether U.S.–Iran diplomacy makes substantive progress and whether major Middle‑East shipping lanes become safe again. If fighting continues, tanker attacks stay high and crude exports face further limits, prices could regain upward pressure; conversely, a diplomatic breakthrough and a gradual restoration of energy transport could dissipate the built‑up geopolitical risk premium.

items.title: 蘋果新掌門蜜月期告終！iPhone Duo熱銷難掩隱憂 Siri追不上AI代理浪潮 記憶體成本成考驗
items.title_en: Apple's New CEO Honeymoon Ends: iPhone Duo Sales Can't Hide Worries as Siri Lags Behind AI Agent Wave and Memory Costs Rise
paras: 蘋果 (Apple) (AAPL-US) 新任執行長約翰·特努斯上任約兩個月，便迎來首款折疊手機iPhone Duo上市的市場考驗。儘管新機需求強勁，帶動蘋果股價走高，但供應鏈瓶頸、記憶體成本飆升，以及人工智慧(AI)發展落後等問題，正逐漸浮上檯面。
特努斯週一首次以執行長身分出席季度財報電話會議，正式面對華爾街分析師。他雖然展現信心，卻有不少問題交由財務長凱文·帕雷克及營運長薩比赫·汗回答。蘋果也表示，兩人未來將固定參與財報電話會議，顯示新管理團隊可能採取更分工的對外溝通方式。
從財務表現來看，蘋果仍處於強勁成長階段。9月iPhone銷量創下歷史紀錄，11月4日股價上漲逾5%，收盤市值達5.08兆美元，重新奪回全球市值第一的位置。
然而，亮眼的銷售數字並未消除市場疑慮。蘋果正面臨記憶體晶片價格急漲、零組件供應受限，以及部分產品必須透過漲價抵銷成本壓力等問題。iPhone Duo雖然開局熱銷，但新訂單出貨時間已延後至明年1月底，反映需求與供應能力之間仍存在明顯落差。
特努斯在財報會議上坦言，目前記憶體晶片價格漲勢「前所未見」，已對產品定價形成壓力。他並預告，截至12月的財季結束後，蘋果採購記憶體的價格仍可能繼續上升。
成本壓力也反映在獲利預測上。蘋果預估12月財季毛利率將降至45%至46%，低於9月財季的47.9%。上一季毛利率約有1個百分點來自關稅退稅，因此若排除這項因素，獲利能力面臨的壓力更值得關注。
蘋果指出，毛利率下滑主要受到記憶體成本持續上升，以及Siri AI研發與部署支出增加影響。換言之，公司不僅必須承擔硬體成本上漲，也需要持續投入資源追趕AI競爭對手。
投資人對此已經提出警告。蘋果投資者吉恩·蒙斯特在財報公布前接受《Fortune》訪問時表示，今年假日購物季的下行風險遠高於上行空間。財報公布後，他又在社群平台X指出，管理層顯然不願深入討論個人化AI代理，而這才是蘋果生態系統面臨的最大風險之一。
AI發展也成為特努斯首次財報會議最受關注的議題之一。當分析師詢問新版Siri的發展方向，以及產業逐漸轉向Meta (META-US)旗下Muse等消費級AI代理的趨勢時，特努斯並未提出明確時程，只表示目前Siri仍主要採取依照使用者指令執行任務的模式，但其底層架構具備進一步擴充能力。
特努斯認為，AI代理對使用者而言具有廣闊前景，但也提醒，使用者必須清楚了解授予AI工具的存取權限，並將安全與隱私列為重要考量。這反映蘋果仍希望以隱私作為產品差異化優勢，但市場更關心的是，公司能否將這項優勢轉化為實際的AI競爭力。
目前新版Siri AI仍以測試版形式推送。蘋果原本將其定位為重要的產品升級，功能包括理解使用者螢幕上的內容、跨應用程式執行操作、協助撰寫文件，以及搜尋裝置內資訊來補足對話脈絡。
不過，新版Siri的市場評價並不一致。部分分析師肯定功能有所進步，但整體能力仍被認為落後於OpenAI及Anthropic等AI業者，也未能跟上Meta等公司推動的個人化AI代理趨勢。新一代AI代理已逐漸具備自行網路購物、查閱銀行帳單等多步驟任務能力，與目前仍以指令回應為主的Siri形成對比。
美國銀行 (Bank of America)分析師瓦姆西·莫漢認為，新版Siri確實更強大、實用，但核心問題在於蘋果準備如何推動下一階段發展。對蘋果而言，AI不只是新增功能，而是攸關使用者是否持續留在其生態系統，以及未來能否創造新收入來源的關鍵。
面對服務業務成長放緩，包括iCloud及App Store等收入來源的增速受到關注，特努斯與其他高階主管則將焦點放在蘋果龐大的使用者基礎。公司全球活躍裝置數量已超過25億台，這些使用者未來有望成為AI服務及訂閱業務變現的基礎。
管理層也透露，對於必須仰賴非本地端AI運算的功能，蘋果將設定一定使用限制；此外，過去主要依照儲存容量分級收費的iCloud訂閱方案，未來也可能調整。這意味蘋果可能重新設計服務收費模式，以支應AI運算成本並開拓新的營收來源。
硬體方面，iPhone Duo是特努斯上任後最受矚目的產品。這款蘋果首款折疊手機於9月初由特努斯首次以執行長身分公開發布，上市後需求強勁，但供應限制使外界難以準確估算實際銷量。
除了交貨延遲，部分iPhone Duo還傳出螢幕開裂問題，蘋果已承認相關情況，並表示將為受影響用戶更換新機。這類品質問題若持續擴大，可能進一步增加新品上市初期的售後成本與品牌壓力。
對於iPhone Duo的產能狀況，特努斯將相關問題交由營運長薩比赫·汗回答。汗表示，產能爬坡整體進展順利，但目前仍難以精確預測供需何時能夠達到平衡。獨立投資研究機構Yorkville Ives則預估，蘋果未來幾季可望售出約1,000萬部iPhone Duo。
蘋果也正在調整iPhone產品發布節奏。新一代iPhone Pro、Pro Max及Duo已於秋季推出，基本款iPhone與新型號iPhone Air則預計延至明年春季上市。美國銀行分析師莫漢認為，分階段發布策略雖然有助於延長產品熱度，但若同時遇上零件成本上漲及服務業務成長放緩，仍可能對未來業績形成壓力。
中國市場則呈現成長與落差並存的情況。蘋果9月財季在大中華區的銷售額年增21%，但《彭博社》估算，實際業績仍比華爾街預期低約10億美元，顯示即使銷售成長強勁，市場對蘋果在中國的復甦程度仍抱持更高期待。
在AI布局方面，蘋果經過長時間談判後，已與阿里巴巴集團 (Alibaba) (BABA-US)達成協議，計畫為中國大陸iPhone用戶推出符合當地市場需求的AI功能。不過，這項合作並不代表中國用戶能夠使用完整版本的Siri AI，蘋果在不同市場提供的AI體驗仍可能存在差異。
整體而言，特努斯接掌蘋果後，確實迎來iPhone Duo熱銷、iPhone銷量創紀錄及市值重返全球第一等利多，但這些成績尚不足以證明新管理團隊已找到下一階段的成長引擎。
短期內，蘋果仍可憑藉超過25億台的活躍裝置，以及強大的品牌與產品生態系統維持營收動能。然而，記憶體成本上漲可能侵蝕毛利率，供應瓶頸也限制新品銷售規模；更長期的挑戰，則是Siri能否從傳統語音助理升級為真正具備自主執行能力的AI代理。
對特努斯而言，真正的考驗並非如何延續iPhone Duo上市初期的熱度，而是能否在硬體成本上升、AI競爭加劇及服務業務成長放緩的環境下，證明蘋果仍有能力創造下一波足以支撐兆美元市值的成長動能。
paras_en: Apple (AAPL-US) new CEO John Ternus, about two months into his tenure, faces the market test of the first foldable iPhone Duo launch. While demand for the new device is strong, boosting Apple’s share price, supply‑chain bottlenecks, soaring memory costs and lagging AI development are coming to the fore.

Ternus appeared for the first time as CEO at the quarterly earnings call on Monday, facing Wall Street analysts. Though he showed confidence, many questions were directed to CFO Kevin Parker and COO Sabih Khan. Apple also said the two will regularly join future earnings calls, suggesting a more divided external communication approach by the new leadership team.

From a financial standpoint Apple remains in a strong growth phase. September iPhone sales hit a record, and on November 4 the stock rose more than 5%, closing at a market cap of $5.08 trillion, reclaiming the world’s top‑valued company spot.

However, the impressive sales numbers have not erased market concerns. Apple is confronting sharply rising memory‑chip prices, limited component supply and the need to raise prices on some products to offset cost pressure. The iPhone Duo sold well out of the gate, but new order shipments have been pushed back to the end of January 2025, highlighting a clear gap between demand and supply capability.

Ternus admitted at the earnings call that memory‑chip price increases are “unprecedented” and are pressuring product pricing. He warned that even after the fiscal quarter ending December, Apple’s memory procurement costs could keep climbing.

Cost pressure is also reflected in profit forecasts. Apple expects the gross margin for the December quarter to fall to 45‑46%, down from 47.9% in the September quarter. About one percentage point of the prior margin came from tariff rebates, so excluding that factor the profit pressure is even more pronounced.

Apple said the margin decline is driven mainly by continued memory‑cost increases and higher Siri AI R&D and deployment spending. In other words, the company must absorb higher hardware costs while also pouring resources into catching up with AI rivals.

Investors have already sounded warnings. Apple investor Gene Monaster told Fortune before the earnings release that the holiday‑season downside risk far outweighs upside potential. After the release he posted on X that management clearly avoids deep discussion of personalized AI agents, which he sees as one of the biggest risks to Apple’s ecosystem.

AI development was one of the most‑watched topics at Ternus’s first earnings briefing. When analysts asked about the direction of the new Siri and the industry shift toward consumer‑grade AI agents like Meta’s (META-US) Muse, Ternus gave no concrete timeline, saying Siri still mainly follows user commands but its underlying architecture is built for future expansion.

Ternus believes AI agents have broad potential for users but cautions that users must understand the permissions they grant AI tools and keep security and privacy front‑and‑center. This reflects Apple’s continued emphasis on privacy as a product differentiator, though the market is more focused on whether that advantage can be turned into real AI competitiveness.

The new Siri AI is currently being rolled out as a beta. Apple originally positioned it as a major product upgrade, with capabilities such as understanding on‑screen content, cross‑app actions, document drafting assistance, and searching device‑stored information to enrich conversational context.

However, market reception to the new Siri is mixed. Some analysts acknowledge functional improvements, but overall capability is still seen as lagging behind AI firms like OpenAI and Anthropic, and it has not kept pace with the personalized AI agent trend driven by companies such as Meta. Next‑gen AI agents now can shop online, review bank statements and perform multi‑step tasks, contrasting with Siri’s current command‑response model.

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan says the new Siri is indeed more powerful and useful, but the core issue is how Apple will drive the next development stage. For Apple, AI is not just a new feature; it is crucial to keeping users in its ecosystem and creating future revenue streams.

Facing slowing growth in services such as iCloud and the App Store, Ternus and other senior executives are focusing on Apple’s massive user base. The company now has over 2.5 billion active devices worldwide, which could become the foundation for monetizing AI services and subscriptions.

Management also disclosed that functions requiring off‑device AI computation will have usage limits, and the traditionally tiered iCloud storage pricing may be revised. This suggests Apple could redesign service pricing to cover AI compute costs and open new revenue sources.

On the hardware side, the iPhone Duo is the most high‑profile product since Ternus took over. Apple’s first foldable phone was unveiled by Ternus in early September, and demand surged after launch, but supply constraints make it hard for outsiders to gauge actual sales volumes.

In addition to delivery delays, some iPhone Duo units have reported screen‑cracking issues; Apple has acknowledged the problem and said affected users will receive replacement devices. If such quality issues expand, they could raise early‑stage after‑sales costs and brand pressure.

When asked about iPhone Duo capacity, Ternus deferred to COO Sabih Khan, who said the production ramp is progressing well overall but it remains difficult to predict when supply and demand will balance. Independent research firm Yorkville Ives estimates Apple could sell roughly 10 million iPhone Duo units over the next few quarters.

Apple is also adjusting its iPhone release cadence. The new iPhone Pro, Pro Max and Duo arrived in the fall, while the standard iPhone and the new iPhone Air are slated for a spring 2025 launch. BofA analyst Mohan believes the staggered rollout helps sustain product momentum, but if component costs keep rising and services growth slows, it could still pressure future results.

China shows a mixed picture of growth and gaps. Apple’s September quarter sales in Greater China rose 21% year‑over‑year, yet Bloomberg estimates actual performance was about $1 billion below Wall Street expectations, indicating that despite strong sales growth, the market still expects a larger recovery in China.

In AI positioning, after lengthy negotiations Apple has struck a deal with Alibaba (BABA-US) to roll out AI features tailored to mainland‑China iPhone users. However, the partnership does not mean Chinese users will get the full Siri AI version; Apple’s AI experience will still vary by market.

Overall, Ternus’s tenure has delivered iPhone Duo hype, record iPhone sales and a return to the top‑valued‑company rank, but these achievements alone do not prove the new team has found the next growth engine.

In the short term Apple can rely on its more than 2.5 billion active devices, strong brand and ecosystem to sustain revenue momentum. Yet rising memory costs may erode margins and supply bottlenecks limit new‑product sales; the longer‑term challenge is whether Siri can evolve from a traditional voice assistant into a truly autonomous AI agent.

For Ternus, the real test is not extending the early buzz of the iPhone Duo launch but proving Apple can generate the next wave of growth that supports a trillion‑plus market cap despite higher hardware costs, intensifying AI competition and slowing services growth.

items.title: 民主黨大獲全勝後 參議員桑德斯呼籲「全美暫停」興建資料中心
items.title_en: After Democrats’ Sweep, Senator Sanders Calls for a Nationwide Pause on Data Center Construction
paras: 美國民主黨在期中選舉大勝後，部分國會議員與新當選州長開始要求限制人工智慧 (AI) 與資料中心擴張。參議員桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 呼籲全美暫停興建資料中心，德州州長當選人希諾霍薩 (Gina Hinojosa) 則曾承諾，上任後將暫停核准所有資料中心開發案。隨著反對聲浪從競選訴求轉向施政主張，市場擔憂相關建設進度可能受阻，帶動 AI 晶片與基礎建設類股遭到拋售。
《CNBC》週四 (5 日) 報導，資料中心的環境影響、資源使用與地方決策權，已成為這次選舉的重要議題。民主黨除了在國會取得優勢，也贏得關鍵州長選戰，使投資人開始重新評估聯邦與州政府政策對 AI 建設熱潮的影響。
桑德斯要求全美暫停建設 進步派議員呼籲優先處理
與民主黨共同運作的佛蒙特州無黨籍參議員桑德斯，在社群平台 X 發文指出，全美多個地方選民週二透過公投支持限制資料中心，已向政治人物傳達明確訊息。
桑德斯呼籲「立即在全國暫停興建資料中心」，並批評大型科技企業寡頭破壞環境、削減工作機會，甚至威脅人類未來。
亞利桑那州民主黨眾議員安薩里 (Yassamin Ansari) 也在 X 發文，主張民主黨取得眾議院大幅多數優勢後，應將暫停 AI 發展列為新會期首日的優先事項。國會進步派黨團主席、德州眾議員卡薩爾 (Greg Casar) 隨後轉發，並表態支持。
這些發言顯示，部分議員的訴求已超出個別資料中心開發案，延伸至更廣泛的 AI 發展限制。不過，全國性暫停建設目前仍是政治倡議，尚未成為已生效的政策。
逾半選民將 AI 與資料中心列為投票考量
民主黨人士推動限制措施的背後，是選民對 AI 與資料中心議題的高度關注。
根據 CNBC 選民調查，56% 的選民表示，AI 與資料中心是影響其投票決定的關鍵或主要因素；在這群選民中，65% 表示將國會選票投給民主黨候選人。
不過，這項調查反映的是議題對投票的影響程度，不能直接解讀為 56% 的選民支持全面禁止資料中心。
多名翻轉關鍵選區的民主黨候選人，也在勝選演說中延續競選期間對科技企業的批評。
在南卡羅來納州贏得聯邦參議員席次的安德魯斯 (Annie Andrews) 表示，選民選擇的是由當地居民決定社區事務，而非交由億萬富豪或資料中心企業左右。
俄亥俄州民主黨人布朗 (Sherrod Brown) 擊敗共和黨現任參議員休斯特德 (Jon Husted)、重返參議院後，也在勝選演說中強調：「我不是替資料中心工作。」
德州成政策焦點 占全美規劃中產能 27%
相較於國會議員的全國性倡議，州政府對資料中心開發的態度，同樣受到市場關注。其中，德州是觀察重點。
根據富國銀行數據，德州占全美規劃中資料中心產能的 27%。因此，當地若暫停核准新案，可能影響相當大一部分待開發計畫。
擊敗共和黨現任州長艾波特 (Greg Abbott) 的民主黨人希諾霍薩，雖未在勝選演說中直接談及資料中心，但曾在 10 月底發布的競選影片中承諾，上任後將暫停所有資料中心開發案的核准，直到州議會通過保護德州居民的法律。
她將資料中心爭議定位為居民與大型資本之間的權力問題，質疑德州究竟應由人民作主，還是成為億萬富豪主導的世界。
賓州州長夏皮洛 (Josh Shapiro) 則已在 8 月簽署行政命令，放慢資料中心開發。他在勝選演說中表示，大型科技企業不應決定居民的未來，地方社區應握有最終決定權。
政策疑慮衝擊 AI 類股 市場關注承諾如何落實
隨著民主黨勝選，市場開始擔憂，聯邦與州層級的限制措施可能拖慢資料中心建設，進而影響晶片、伺服器及其他基礎建設需求。
與 AI 建設相關的股票在選後週三已出現跌勢，週四賣壓進一步加劇，晶片股陷入大逃殺，費半指數狂瀉超 12%。
接下來的關鍵，在於這些競選承諾與政治倡議，將以何種範圍及形式落實。桑德斯提出的是全國性暫停建設，希諾霍薩主張暫停德州新案核准，夏皮洛則強調放慢開發並保障地方決策權，各項措施的影響並不相同。
對 AI 供應鏈而言，政策風險已成為投資人評估成長前景的新變數；實際衝擊仍取決於限制措施是否實施，以及涵蓋哪些開發計畫。
paras_en: After the Democratic Party’s landslide victory in the midterm elections, some members of Congress and newly elected governors have begun calling for limits on artificial intelligence (AI) and data‑center expansion. Senator Bernie Sanders urged a nationwide pause on building data centers, while Texas governor‑elect Gina Hinojosa pledged to halt approval of all data‑center projects once in office. As opposition shifts from campaign rhetoric to policy proposals, markets worry that construction progress could be delayed, prompting a sell‑off in AI‑chip and infrastructure stocks.

CNBC reported on Thursday the 5th that the environmental impact, resource use, and local decision‑making authority of data centers have become key issues in this election. In addition to gaining a congressional advantage, Democrats also won crucial governor races, leading investors to reassess how federal and state policies might affect the AI construction boom.
Sanders demands a nationwide construction pause; progressive lawmakers call for priority handling

Working with the Democratic Party, independent Vermont Senator Sanders posted on X that voters in multiple locales voted on Tuesday in referendums to limit data centers, sending a clear message to politicians.
Sanders called for an “immediate nationwide pause on data‑center construction,” criticizing big‑tech oligarchs for harming the environment, cutting jobs, and even threatening humanity’s future.

Arizona Democratic Representative Yassamin Ansari also posted on X, arguing that after Democrats secure a large House majority, a pause on AI development should be a top priority on the first day of the new session. House Progressive Caucus chair and Texas Representative Greg Casar retweeted and voiced support.

These statements show that some lawmakers’ demands go beyond individual data‑center projects to broader AI development restrictions. However, a nationwide construction halt remains a political proposal and has not become an enforceable policy yet.
More than half of voters consider AI and data centers when voting
Democratic advocates are pushing restrictions because voters are highly attentive to AI and data‑center issues.

According to a CNBC poll, 56% of respondents said AI and data centers were a key or major factor influencing their vote; among those voters, 65% said they would cast their congressional ballot for a Democratic candidate.
The poll reflects the issue’s impact on voting behavior and should not be interpreted as 56% of voters supporting a total ban on data centers.
Several Democratic candidates who flipped key swing districts continued their campaign‑time criticism of tech firms in their victory speeches.
In South Carolina, newly elected Senator Annie Andrews said voters chose local residents to decide community matters rather than billionaires or data‑center companies.
Ohio Democrat Sherrod Brown, who defeated incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, reiterated in his victory speech, “I’m not working for data centers.”
Texas becomes a policy focus, accounting for 27% of planned U.S. capacity
Compared with the nationwide push by members of Congress, state governments’ stances on data‑center development also attract market attention, with Texas being a key focus.

Wells Fargo data show Texas accounts for 27% of the United States’ planned data‑center capacity. Consequently, a state‑level pause on new approvals could affect a substantial portion of pending projects.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, did not mention data centers in her victory speech but promised in a campaign video released at the end of October to suspend all data‑center approvals until the state legislature passes a law protecting Texas residents.
She framed the data‑center debate as a power struggle between residents and large capital, questioning whether Texas should be governed by its people or become a playground for billionaires.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed an executive order in August to slow data‑center development. In his victory speech he said large tech firms should not decide residents’ futures and that local communities must retain final authority.
Policy concerns are hitting AI‑related stocks, and markets are watching how promises will be implemented
With Democrats in power, markets are worried that federal and state restrictions could slow data‑center construction, dampening demand for chips, servers, and other infrastructure components.
AI‑related stocks slipped on the Wednesday after the election, and selling pressure intensified on Thursday, sending chip shares into a sharp sell‑off and the Nasdaq‑100 index plunging more than 12%.

The next key question is how these campaign promises and political initiatives will be realized in scope and form. Sanders proposes a nationwide construction pause, Hinojosa seeks to halt new Texas approvals, and Shapiro emphasizes slowing development while safeguarding local decision‑making; each measure would have different impacts.

For the AI supply chain, policy risk has become a new variable investors consider when evaluating growth prospects; the actual impact will depend on whether restrictions are enacted and which projects they cover.
